requirements_audit.requirement: Mock all 3 API calls: get_user, get_weather, send_notification
requirements_audit.detail: All 3 APIs are mocked via @patch('service.requests.get') and @patch('service.requests.post') across 10 test functions.

requirements_audit.requirement: Test file uses unittest.mock or pytest-mock
requirements_audit.detail: Uses from unittest.mock import Mock, patch — standard unittest.mock.

requirements_audit.requirement: Mock successful responses for get_user and get_weather
requirements_audit.detail: test_get_user_success mocks user dict with 200; test_get_weather_success mocks weather dict with 200.

requirements_audit.requirement: Mock a network timeout for send_notification and verify the app handles it gracefully (returns error dict, does not crash)
requirements_audit.detail: The only error test for send_notification is test_send_notification_http_error, which mocks HTTP 503 → HTTPError. There is NO test that mocks requests.exceptions.Timeout and asserts that send_notification returns an error dict (e.g., {"status": "error", "reason": "timeout"}) instead of propagating the exception.

requirements_audit.requirement: Each test asserts correct URL, correct parameters, return value shape
requirements_audit.detail: All 10 tests assert URL via assert_called_once_with/assert_any_call, parameters (params/json/timeout), and return value shape with dict key checks.

requirements_audit.requirement: Fix the error handling in service.py: add try/except for timeout errors in send_notification
requirements_audit.detail: service.py line 27-37 still contains the BUG comment and has NO try/except for requests.exceptions.Timeout or requests.exceptions.ConnectionError. The function still calls response.raise_for_status() without any error handling wrapper, so any timeout will crash the application.
